native_assumptions.description: Generate exactly 3000 complete rows, with synthetic identifiers, integer age 35 through 74 inclusive, female 0/1, positive BMI, serum glucose and HbA1c percent. These are task requirements; rows do not represent recovered people or a survey-weighted population.
Age is discrete uniform on all 40 task-eligible integer years. No target composition is supplied. This is a composition assumption, not a restriction or fit imported from any source.

Use the MIND-China BMI, FSG and HbA1c mean/individual-SD pairs and female count fraction as plug-in marginal anchors for a target scenario. MIND includes known diabetes and measures serum glucose, which motivates choosing it over sources excluding prior diabetes or using plasma. Transport remains unsupported across rural older adults aged 61-80 in 2019, selected dementia/disability-free follow-up with prior-year BMI and imputation, to the 35-74-year 2009 released-data analytical population. No age reweighting, diabetes-state adjustment, national weighting, treatment exclusion or recovery of missing participants is asserted.

The target glucose variable denotes central-serum glucose, in mmol/L. The model adopts the MIND FSG mean and individual SD on that scale, assuming transferable serum-assay and processing behavior. It does not alias plasma FPG to FSG, infer a serum/plasma correction, impose a source fasting duration on the target, or claim assay equivalence. HbA1c is in percent; no IFCC conversion is used in generation.

Each continuous variable follows its own positive lognormal distribution. Its two parameters are algebraically determined by the selected source mean and individual SD. The shape and tails are modeling choices; two marginal moments do not identify a lognormal law. No clinical upper/lower cutoff, mixture, clipping, truncation, rejection or diabetes exclusion is introduced.

Age, female, BMI, serum glucose and HbA1c are mutually independent within a row; rows are IID conditional on the fixed specification. E0 contains no numerical relationship records. Independence is an explicit, parsimonious completion assumption, not evidence that associations are absent. It forces the three requested population OLS focal coefficients to zero and precludes empirical claims about those associations.

Published individual SDs describe person-to-person dispersion, not SEs. Treat selected source means, SDs and count fraction as fixed plug-in settings. No source estimator uncertainty, precision weighting, confidence interval, or Bayesian probability is manufactured. The same source mean/SD pair and its derived lognormal parameters are not independent evidence.

The execution adapter can produce only the target table. No source-population input, source-covariate reconstruction or replay is allocated. Every source comparison is therefore unavailable even where a source definition is known. Target rows or analytic target-law moments are not source-population checks.

The seed controls a NumPy default_rng pseudo-random implementation of the declared IID law. No sample centering, SD matching, re-ranking, coefficient correction, favorable seed selection or resampling on diagnostic results occurs. A nonfinite or nonpositive continuous value fails the run rather than being clipped or redrawn.

Transport the three MIND mean/individual-SD pairs for BMI, fasting serum glucose, and HbA1c percent as chosen marginal anchors. Its age, selection, date, prior-year BMI, imputation, assay and fasting context still differ.

Each continuous margin is lognormal with log variance log(1+(SD/mean)^2) and log mean log(mean)-log variance/2. A lognormal tail and strictly positive support are author assumptions; the source mean and SD do not identify the family. No clipping, row rejection or diabetes exclusion is applied. Unbounded tails are not validated physiological extremes; in particular no HbA1c upper bound is supplied by the task.

A common independent standard-normal factor has standardized log-scale loadings 0.30 for BMI, 0.60 for glucose and 0.70 for HbA1c. Each margin has its own independent normal residual with loading sqrt(1-loading^2). These positive associations and exact loadings are explicit illustrative assumptions, not reported evidence, calibrated estimates, or a favored target direction. Marginal evidence alone cannot choose them.

Age and female are independent of each other and of the common factor and all continuous residuals. This simplifying assumption is unsupported by E0 relationship evidence, which is absent rather than evidence of zero. It algebraically fixes the population age coefficient in E3 at zero and fixes age/female slopes in E1/E2 at zero. Finite-sample coefficients fluctuate.

MIND serum FSG remains distinct from the plasma FPG in Jansen and Bao. Native target serum glucose is modeled directly in mmol/L with no plasma conversion; HbA1c percent is used directly. No NGSP conversion is needed. Matching unit labels does not establish assay or population equivalence. There is no diabetes, pregnancy or treatment exclusion and no target data.

Reported individual SDs set individual variation under the assumed law, not estimator SEs, transport tolerances, or weights. Estimator uncertainty and field-specific counts remain unreported. All scientific parameters are held fixed across seeds; seeds vary individual synthetic residuals only. Structural, external-estimate and transport uncertainty are not integrated probabilistically and must be assessed with separately justified future scenarios.

No source-population reconstruction or source replay is supplied. Every target-table source comparison is unavailable. Jansen, Bao and MIND are distinct source families; multiple summaries from each study share that cohort and are not independent replications. No cross-source precision pooling or statistical independence of source estimates is assumed.

The slope identity holds for any finite-variance nondegenerate age law under the stated conditional equation. No complex-survey reconstruction or source age-band calibration is claimed.

native_assumptions.description: The task is an equal-stratum analytical design: each sex crossed with integer age bands 25-39,40-54,55-69,70-79 has exactly375 rows. Within each cell age is uniform over integers, fictional independent individuals conditional on fixed stratum assignments. Not national prevalence weights.

A qualified Lifelines source law uses independent age Uniform(55.5-sqrt(3)*9.9,55.5+sqrt(3)*9.9) and female Bernoulli(0.597). It reproduces admitted marginal moments but not the actual age distribution, GWAS recruitment or Table2 row-specific cases. Table1 and Table2 are treated as representing the same law as an unverified completion assumption.

A qualified Pani NHANES population law uses independent integer age Uniform{25,...,84} and female Bernoulli(0.5), with the same conditional equations as the target and Lifelines law. The upper age84 is an explicit technical source-completion assumption, not an admitted source cutoff. In particular the reported >=70 band is approximated by70-84. Uniform age weights and sex balance are assumed population probabilities, not source survey weights or counts.

BMI and glucose conditional means have assumed age slopes0.04 kg/m^2/year and0.12 mg/dL/year and female-minus-male shifts0.4 kg/m^2 and-2 mg/dL. Residual correlation0.30 is an unsupported completion choice; it is not identified by the two Jansen projections. Demographic independence and zero other latent cross-covariances are structural assumptions, not absence-of-evidence facts.

Three independent standardized symmetric Beta(3,3) variables drive BMI, glucose and HbA1c residuals. Each has mean0, variance1 and support[-sqrt(7),sqrt(7)]. This is an assumed bounded, continuous, symmetric residual law; its support is a modeling limitation, not a population cutoff. No clipping or rejection is performed.

Conditional HbA1c expectation is additive and linear in age, female, BMI and glucose, with constant independent residual variance and no interactions. Direct female coefficient0 is an explicit simplifying assumption. This conditional equation is an associational law, not a causal structural claim.

Jansen locations, variation and separate BMI/glucose projections and the Pani adjusted age association are transported to one common conditional law. Source ancestry, age distributions, source row exclusions, plasma versus target serum glucose, assays, fasting duration, pregnancy routing, anemia and medication differences are unverified. Common coefficients across sources and the task are assumptions; no target statistic was available.

The law describes an already eligible analytical population; non-diabetes diagnosis,8-12-hour fast, standing anthropometry consistency and routed pregnancy/lactation exclusions are membership premises, not simulated measured flags. It includes no verified anemia or medication exclusion. All generated glucose is positive and<126 by derived support, not an HbA1c diagnostic screen.

External estimates are fixed plug-in anchors. The unknown-level Jansen printed interval bounds and Pani P value do not yield SEs. Pani age-band SEs quantify source survey estimate uncertainty, not individual dispersion. Seeds change individual residual realizations, not external-estimate, structural or transport uncertainty.

Jansen Table1 and Table2 belong to Lifelines and are not independent studies. Original and converted versions are single quantities. Pani slope and age-band means are one NHANES source, potentially overlapping other NHANES reports; no such other report is used. Pani FOS results are not pooled. No cross-study uncertainty independence is claimed.
